# Candidate-screening double-comma regression fixture (P0-02)

This fixture captures the reported candidate-detector failure so it stays
reproducible. `source.docx` is regenerated by `build_fixture.py`; the paragraphs
and the expectations below are the golden record.

> Note: the original incident's job artifacts (the exact manuscript, output
> document, ledger, report) were not available to this branch. This is a
> **minimal, deterministic reproduction of the same failure mode**, distilled
> from the root-cause analysis. It reproduces every observed double-comma edit.

## The failure

The introductory-clause branch of `_introductory_candidates`
(`docproof/candidate_generators.py`) placed a **zero-width insertion anchor with
`observed_text=""`** and `correction=","`, `channel="edit"`. Two distinct bugs
followed:

1. **Double comma on already-correct clauses.** For a clause that already had
   its comma, the anchor landed *directly on top of the existing comma*
   (`start == end == boundary + comma.start()`). Applying the correction spliced
   in a second comma.
2. **Mis-located comma on genuinely-missing clauses.** When no comma existed,
   the anchor fell back to `boundary` — the position immediately after the
   conjunction — so the comma was inserted in the wrong place.

Because `observed_text` was empty, `validate_candidate_anchor` compared
`para.text[start:start] == ""`, which is true at every offset, so the stale
anchor could never be caught (P1-03), and there was no guard rejecting an
insertion adjacent to identical punctuation (P1-02) nor any final-document
invariant catching `",,"` (P1-04).

## Observed edits, pre-fix (confirmed against the generator)

| Paragraph | Anchor | Applied result (WRONG) |
|---|---|---|
| `After the war, the men returned home.` | (13,13) insert `,` | `After the war,, the men returned home.` |
| `Although she was tired, she kept walking.` | (22,22) insert `,` | `Although she was tired,, she kept walking.` |
| `Because it rained, the match was cancelled.` | (17,17) insert `,` | `Because it rained,, the match was cancelled.` |
| `When the sun rose the birds sang.` | (4,4) insert `,` | `When, the sun rose the birds sang.` |

## Expected behaviour, post-fix

- **Correctly punctuated clauses** (`After the war, …`, `Although she was
  tired, …`, `Because it rained, …`, `Meanwhile, …`): the existing comma is
  anchored as observed text and classified a **pass** — no candidate correction,
  no edit.
- **Genuinely missing intro-clause comma** (`When the sun rose the birds
  sang.`): the deterministic generator cannot locate the true clause boundary
  without a parser, so it **fails closed** — surfaced as a non-editing query,
  never a wrong-location comma insertion. (A parser-backed generator, P2-05, may
  later locate the boundary and propose the edit.)
- **Strong single-word intro missing its comma** (`However he never arrived.`):
  the comma belongs immediately after the transitional adverb, so this remains a
  safe insertion at `boundary`.
- **Universal safety net**: even if any generator regresses, the insertion guard
  (P1-02) and the final-document invariant (P1-04) reject any edit that would
  create adjacent duplicate punctuation.

The regression is exercised by `tests/test_candidate_double_comma.py`.
